title: City of Edmonton enforcement order and Council appeal decision: fire alarm, exit and egress deficiencies in an assembly building with later additions (Council Order 2023-08)
jurisdiction: City of Edmonton, Alberta (City named as the issuing authority in the order)
code_edition: unknown if unstated for the 2020 permit; the decision cites NBC(AE) 2019 Division B 8.2.1 (p.8) and NFPA 96 for kitchen exhaust (p.8)
document_date: Hearing 2023-12-11; decision signed 2024-02-07; City order 2023-03-30; varied by Provincial Administrator 2023-04-17

facts.text: The City of Edmonton issued an order on 2023-03-30 to the Siri Guru Nanak Sikh Gurdwara of Alberta; the Provincial Administrator varied it on 2023-04-17.
The Tribunal hearing was held virtually on 2023-12-11. The appellants did not appear; it was the third scheduled hearing date after two adjournment requests, and reminder emails went unanswered.
A Commercial Final Permit issued 2020-09-01 for the addition carried conditions including no rooms for sleeping and a maximum occupant load of 280 persons.

The First Inspection Report listed the fire alarm as non-operational and not extended into the south addition, exit signage missing in the south addition and basement, kick-down hold-open devices on exit stair doors, and missing fire-separation doors.
The same report lists the south-west exit stairwell egress blocked by stored combustible material and the north basement exit stairs obstructed and not operational.
The decision records a central basement assembly area developed without permit and without ventilation, plus kitchen exhaust clearance and duct-slope problems under NFPA 96.

The Tribunal states the City 'has focused on life safety only' (para 94), and that 'the Varied Second Order is upheld' (para 95). The operative paragraph requires the appellants to cease use, vacate and secure the building by 2024-02-11, and within 21 days to obtain permits for completed work to restore a safe condition; the extract also shows an alternative (c) to remove the additions and restore the last permitted state.

limitations: Regulatory appeal decision, not an alternative-solution submission or design report. Inspection findings are the City's account as recited in the decision.
